text.en: Meena found a toy labelled 'Made in China'. "Why are goods from everywhere?" she asked.

Globalisation links places through trade, investment, technology and communication. South India took part in trade across the Indian Ocean long before 1991. The reforms of 1991 were an important change in India’s economic policies.
International trade is the exchange of goods and services across borders. WTO member governments negotiate agreements and use the organisation’s forums to discuss trade issues. A multinational enterprise operates in more than one country. Foreign direct investment involves a lasting interest in an enterprise in another economy.
Trade and investment can create opportunities, but the effects on producers, workers and consumers differ. The trade balance compares export and import values. Other evidence is needed to assess working conditions, local opportunities and the distribution of gains.
Globalisation means countries are linked through trade, investment and technology.

board.text: globalisation

text.en: Cross-border trade is much older than the reforms of nineteen ninety-one. That year marked an important shift in India’s trade and investment policies.

board.text: liberalisation

text.en: International trade is the exchange of goods and services across national borders. The World Trade Organization provides a forum for member governments to negotiate and apply agreed trade rules.

board.text: WTO

text.en: A multinational enterprise operates in more than one country. Its activities can include factories, offices or service centres.

board.text: multinational company

text.en: Foreign direct investment involves a lasting interest by an investor based in one economy in a business in another economy. It can bring capital and skills, though effects differ.

board.text: FDI

text.en: Globalisation can widen consumer choice, open markets and create some jobs. It can also expose firms and workers to pressures from competition.

board.text: trade

text.en: A trade balance compares export and import values over a period. Judging the effects of trade also requires information about jobs, prices and local industries.

board.text: globalisation

text.en: Products, investment, information and services can move across borders. These connections make events in one place matter to people elsewhere.

board.text: Globalisation means growing connections

text.en: Merchants used land and ocean routes long before modern containers and the internet. Older networks moved goods, ideas and people.

board.text: Global connections have a long history

text.en: Ports and merchants linked South India with other regions. Records and archaeological finds help historians understand those connections.

board.text: South India traded across the Indian Ocean

text.en: Ships, railways, containers and quicker communication can link distant producers and customers. They can shorten delivery or coordination time.

board.text: Transport and communication changed the scale

text.en: Trade during colonial rule took place under unequal political power. Export patterns and rules could serve the priorities of the ruling power.

board.text: Colonial trade did not benefit everyone equally

text.en: Moving goods between places in India is domestic trade. Selling those goods across a national border is international trade.

board.text: Domestic trade stays within one country

text.en: When an Indian seller sends goods to a buyer abroad, that is an export for India. The same shipment is an import for the buyer’s country.

board.text: Exports and imports depend on viewpoint

text.en: A company may provide design or software work to a customer abroad. In that case the transaction can be trade in services.

board.text: Services can also cross borders

text.en: A product may use materials from one country, be assembled in another and be sold in a third. Its full supply chain involves several places.

board.text: A supply chain links stages of production

text.en: Tariffs can affect imported prices and competition. Effects depend on the rate, the product and who pays the extra cost.

board.text: A tariff is a tax on imported goods

text.en: Removing or reducing selected restrictions can make it easier for firms to trade or invest. The term does not mean that all rules end.

board.text: Liberalisation changes restrictions

text.en: India introduced a set of economic reforms that changed trade and investment rules. This expanded some existing international links.

board.text: Nineteen ninety-one was a policy turning point

text.en: A firm may distribute production, design or services across several economies. It can coordinate the stages as one business.

board.text: A multinational can organise work across countries

text.en: Selling one order to an overseas customer is trade. A lasting stake in a business in another economy is foreign direct investment.

board.text: Direct investment differs from an ordinary sale

text.en: Investment can create jobs or introduce skills. Local outcomes also depend on working conditions, competition and the links firms build with local suppliers.

board.text: Investment can bring both opportunities and pressures

text.en: The World Trade Organization provides a place for its members to negotiate and discuss how agreed rules apply.

board.text: Member governments negotiate WTO agreements

text.en: Agreements can define what governments have committed to do. Member governments can raise disagreements under agreed procedures.

board.text: Trade rules can make expectations more predictable

text.en: Say which trade you are measuring, for example goods, and use the same currency and period. Subtract import value from export value.

board.text: Trade balance compares exports and imports

text.en: If goods exports are one hundred and twenty and imports are one hundred, the goods balance is plus twenty. If the values are reversed, it is minus twenty.

board.text: A deficit means imports exceed exports in the measure

text.en: The balance does not show whether a workplace is safe, who gained new opportunities, or how much pollution was produced.

board.text: A trade balance can miss important effects

text.en: A buyer can ask how producers are paid and how workers are treated. A claim about fairness should be supported by evidence.

board.text: Fair trade questions include price and working conditions

text.en: Some reach new customers, while others face stronger competition. Access to finance, infrastructure and skills can shape the result.

board.text: Small producers face different opportunities

text.en: A cheaper product can benefit consumers while putting pressure on some local producers. Use several measures to discuss these effects together.

board.text: Compare gains, costs and who receives them

problem.en: What are the benefits of globalisation?

text.en: More choice for consumers.
Jobs and technology.
Wider markets for producers.

problem.en: A Tamil Nadu producer sells cloth to a buyer in another country. How does each side record the shipment?

text.en: For India, goods have been sold abroad.

why.en: It is recorded as an export from the seller’s economy.

text.en: For the buyer’s country, the same goods arrived from abroad.

why.en: It is an import in that economy.

problem.en: Goods exports are 120 units of money and imports are 100. What is the goods trade balance?

text.en: Use export value minus import value.

why.en: Both values cover the same period and category.

text.en: 120 − 100 = +20, a goods trade surplus.

why.en: The sign is positive because exports exceed imports.

problem.en: Which is FDI: selling one batch of goods overseas or taking a lasting stake in an overseas factory?

text.en: The batch sale is a trade transaction.

why.en: It transfers goods but need not create an ongoing business interest.

text.en: The lasting factory stake is an example of foreign direct investment.

why.en: It involves an ongoing interest in an enterprise in another economy.

WTO members negotiate trade rules and agreements.
FDI involves a lasting interest in a business in another economy.
